title: Rhetoric of the Pulpit
welcome_lead: From political speeches to corporate emails, influential power lures rather than commands. Trace the persuasive sinews.
meta_desc: Explore influential power, rhetorical devices and persuasive lexis at A-Level English Language.
final_note: You have unpicked the velvet glove of influential power — persuasion that wears the mask of choice.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Blair's education, education, education uses tricolon to make policy memorable. Three beats lodge a slogan in memory while signalling resolve.

Combined with asyndeton (no conjunctions) the device accelerates pace and projects conviction.

walkthroughs.h2: We, They and the Manufactured Us
walkthroughs.body_html:
Political rhetoric weaponises pronouns. Inclusive we binds speaker and audience into a shared identity; they externalises blame.

Fairclough notes this as a key resource for hegemonic consensus — listeners are positioned inside the speaker's worldview before they evaluate the argument.

High-modality assertions (We will deliver) project certainty; hedged forms (We might consider) signal evasion.

Analysing modality reveals how speakers manage commitment and project competence without bald-on-record force.

mcqs.q: What did Chomsky propose about language acquisition?
options: Children possess an innate Language Acquisition Device — an inborn capacity for grammar — because exposure alone cannot account for how rapidly and uniformly children learn complex syntax.
Chomsky said children should be taught grammar from age two.
Chomsky said children learn language entirely by copying adults.
Skinner believed children couldn't learn language until age five.

mcqs.q: What is Skinner's behaviourist view of language acquisition?
options: Skinner believed children couldn't learn language until age five.
Skinner believed in an innate grammar module.
Children learn language through imitation and operant conditioning — they are reinforced for correct utterances and corrected for errors.
Vygotsky was a behaviourist who emphasised reinforcement.

mcqs.q: What is Vygotsky's view of language development?
options: Language develops through social interaction with more knowledgeable others — they 'scaffold' the child within the Zone of Proximal Development.
Vygotsky believed children develop language alone through internal processes.
Vygotsky was a behaviourist who emphasised reinforcement.
Skinner believed children couldn't learn language until age five.
